content_units: You already have a credible base for an operations-management transition. With 6 years in manufacturing and skills in Lean, root cause analysis, supplier coordination, and basic Power BI, the most realistic path is   operations roles tied to manufacturing, supply chain, industrial operations, or plant performance   rather than jumping straight into broad corporate strategy or general management.
- Best strategy: move through   adjacent operations roles   where your manufacturing credibility is an advantage
Roles to Target and Likely Fit
Role   Why it fits your background   Salary fit vs target   Main gap to close   Realistic in 9 months

Operations Manager (manufacturing/site)   Strong match for Lean, RCA, supplier coordination, process improvement   Often within range at mid-level firms   Team leadership breadth; KPI ownership; budgeting   Yes

Production / Manufacturing Operations Manager   Most direct step from mechanical manufacturing experience   Often within range, especially with shift/site responsibility   People management; planning; cost control   Yes

Continuous Improvement Manager / Operational Excellence Lead   Lean and RCA are directly relevant   Can fit range, especially in larger firms   Broader business impact framing; change management   Yes
Supply Chain Operations Manager   Supplier coordination gives you entry point   Can fit range depending on scope   Inventory, S&OP, logistics, service-level metrics   Yes, with focused upskilling

Program Manager, Industrial Operations   Good if you can show cross-functional delivery   Often near range in MNCs   Structured stakeholder management; project governance   Yes, if positioned carefully
Plant Performance / Site Excellence Lead   Strong for process, yield, downtime, OEE improvement   Often in range in advanced manufacturing   Financial acumen; influencing without authority   Yes
These roles best preserve your domain advantage while moving you toward operations management.

Months 1-2   Reposition your profile for operations   Rewrite CV and LinkedIn around business outcomes; convert engineering tasks into operations metrics; define 20 target companies   Operations-focused resume, LinkedIn, target-company list

Months 2-3   Close the highest-impact skill gaps   Build working knowledge of finance for operations, planning, KPI design, advanced Power BI storytelling; learn Singapore market expectations   2-3 mini-projects and sharper interview stories

Months 3-4   Add visible credibility without full-time study   Complete short certifications or practical courses in operations, supply chain, project leadership, Excel/Power BI   Certificate stack plus portfolio artifacts

Months 4-6   Build market traction   Start targeted applications; reach out to hiring managers and recruiters; conduct informational outreach; tailor resumes by role family   30-50 targeted applications, 15-20 networking conversations

Months 5-7   Prove management readiness   Prepare STAR stories on cost, throughput, quality, suppliers, downtime, and cross-functional leadership; practice case-style ops interviews   Interview-ready narrative and quantified examples

Months 6-9   Convert into offer   Focus on roles with the best salary match; negotiate using scope and impact; prioritize firms where manufacturing ops is core   Offer in target role or near-adjacent stepping-stone role
This is the biggest gap for many engineers moving into management.
- OEE, scrap, yield, OTIF, forecast accuracy, working capital
-   Business impact language gets you hired
Even if you were not a formal manager, you need stories showing:
Hiring teams for operations management often care more about   leadership in practice   than title alone.
For operations roles in Singapore, employers often expect some exposure to:
Your basic Power BI is a good start. Upgrade it to:
You do not need to become a data specialist. You need to show you can   turn plant data into management decisions  .
You should be able to present:
This is often what separates senior engineers from managers.
- Supply chain operations in manufacturing firms
These sectors in Singapore are more likely to value your technical manufacturing background and pay near your target range.
What to Put on Your Resume
Shift from task descriptions to business outcomes.

Mechanical engineer with 6 years in manufacturing, experienced in Lean improvement, root cause analysis, supplier coordination, and performance reporting, now targeting operations management roles focused on productivity, quality, delivery, and cross-functional execution.
- Performed root cause analysis on production issues
- Led root cause investigations that reduced recurring production issues, improved line stability, and supported on-time delivery targets
- Managed supplier coordination to reduce material delays, improve schedule adherence, and support production continuity
- Built Power BI dashboards for operations KPIs, enabling faster issue visibility and management review of downtime, defects, and output trends
- Short online courses in finance for non-finance managers
- Learn how plant KPIs link to profit and working capital
- Inventory, planning, service levels, supplier performance
- Enough to qualify for hybrid ops/supply-chain roles
- One portfolio dashboard based on manufacturing KPIs
- Lightweight certification or training in project execution or operational excellence
- Useful if you target program or transformation roles
Realistic Positioning Against Your Salary Goal
Your target of   SGD 90,000-120,000   is realistic if:
- You target   adjacent management roles  , not head-of-function roles
- You demonstrate people/process ownership, not only technical execution
- You focus on sectors where operations is core and revenue-linked
Most realistic paths to that pay band:
- Move directly into a   manager   title at a mid-sized manufacturer
- Enter a larger firm as   senior specialist / lead in operational excellence or plant performance  , then progress quickly
- Take a role with broad scope over production, suppliers, and KPIs even if the title is not perfect
- If initial offers come slightly below target, a role with stronger title/scope can still be worth taking if it sets up a 12-18 month jump.
- Rebuild CV for operations outcomes, not engineering tasks
- Update LinkedIn headline toward operations/plant performance
- Upgrade Power BI into one polished operations dashboard
- Practice explaining KPI trade-offs: output, quality, cost, delivery
- Build examples of leadership, conflict handling, escalation management
- Take one short course in supply chain or operations leadership
- Start networking with ops managers, recruiters, and ex-colleagues in Singapore
- Apply to 8-12 tailored roles per month
- Focus on operations manager, CI manager, plant performance, and supply chain operations roles
- Refine your pitch based on recruiter feedback
- Prepare answers on team leadership, cost savings, planning, and supplier risk
- Practice salary framing tied to scope and measurable impact
- Prioritize roles closest to target compensation and strongest growth path
- Negotiate on total package, scope, and title
- Accept the best adjacent role if it creates a clear path to full operations ownership
